official_name: Forum of Incident Response and Security Teams

match_nodes.description: Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS): methodology for scoring the severity of software vulnerabilities. Produces a numerical score (0.0-10.0) and severity rating from a set of metrics. Version is significant — CVSS versions differ materially in metric groups and scoring algorithms; v3.1 and v4.0 produce different scores for the same vulnerability, so always specify version.

versions_available.note: Current version. Adds Supplemental metric group, renames Temporal to Threat.
Still widely used. Minor revision of 3.0 with improved guidance.
Legacy. Still seen in older vulnerability databases.

aliases.note: Major-version-only form, widely used in legacy vulnerability data. Resolves both via `@version` (`cvss@2`, canonicalized to `cvss@2.0`) and via the child subpath-document node's pattern (`^2$`, `cvss#2`).

Major-version-only form, widely used in legacy vulnerability data. Resolves both via `@version` (`cvss@1`, canonicalized to `cvss@1.0`) and via the child subpath-document node's pattern (`^1$`, `cvss#1`).

children.description: CVSS v4.0: released 2023. Adds Supplemental metric group, refines Temporal into Threat, adds granularity to Environmental metrics.
CVSS v3.1: released 2019. Widely adopted. Base, Temporal, and Environmental metric groups.
CVSS v3.0: released 2015. First major restructure (Base, Temporal, and Environmental metric groups). Superseded by v3.1.
CVSS v2: released 2007. Refined v1's approach. Largely superseded by v3.x; still appears in legacy data and older NVD records.
CVSS v1: released 2005. Original methodology, the first published version. Deprecated; rarely encountered today.

match_nodes.description: Exploit Prediction Scoring System (EPSS): data-driven methodology for estimating the probability that a software vulnerability will be exploited in the wild within 30 days.
Traffic Light Protocol (TLP): information sharing classification methodology. Defines four levels (RED, AMBER+STRICT, AMBER, GREEN, CLEAR) for marking sensitivity of shared information.
